title: Switching to guitar in 1943-44 and bringing an amplifier
summary: He switched to guitar in 1943 or 44, and at Parisian Gardens Big Joe told him to bring his amplifier despite the pianist's objections.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: You must have switched to guitar in the 30s sometimes.
No I switched to guitar in 1943 or 44. I got the guitar back there. I can go get it and shit.
And then did you start playing electric guitar right away?
No. I was working down there with John Patterson and they told me don't use an amplifier with the guitar so if I'm making bad chords.
That was even when you were starting out on the guitar.
Well I was pretty good. I thought I was good, you understand?
In other words when you switched the guitar they all let it down to fire.
I used to bring the banjo, yeah, but they wouldn't let me use the banjo. You know Miss Kimmel used to kick about it, that thing would probably, you know. So uh.

Yeah. So uh. Big Joe, you know this what you call them, that run the place, he said, how don't you have an amplifier? I said, yes sir. He said, bring it. I said, well they told me not to bring it. He said, this is my place, bring it. So after I started bringing it, at the time she'd go stay one in two hours, you understand, or out on Connell Street, you know. Miss Kimmel? Yeah. She didn't like it. No it wasn't that. She was glad to get a relief. See it was similar to a jitney job. You know during that time we used to have musicians come in there from the NBC, from all over, they would come in there and rest us up. You know there was uniform, there was sailors in different parts of the government where they would be stationed there or near there, they would come in for the weekends and they'd come up there, well I had a chance to pick up an idea from this one, and things like that. Yeah.
